title: rera_project_rows.jsonl — RERA project listing row
description: One project from a state RERA (Real Estate Regulatory Authority) portal's project listing. The shared core is thin on purpose: every column the portal publishes is kept verbatim in `fields`, keyed by the portal's own header string, so nothing is lost and no state's columns are normalized into another's. The typed properties carry only columns that a live capture confirmed (Karnataka and Haryana, November 2026); `additionalProperties` stays true so later states can add their own. `approved_on` is the date the portal prints for the registration: Karnataka's APPROVED ON column, and the date in Haryana's registration certificate number (`... DATED dd.mm.yyyy`), which the Haryana portal has no separate column for. `registration_valid_until` is the date the registration runs to (Haryana's Registration Up-to column). `lapsed` is true when the portal flags the project as lapsed (Haryana prints `Lapsed Project` beside the certificate number); it is absent for a portal with no such flag. The probe records the dates the portal publishes and never computes delay: the gap between the original and the current proposed completion date is interpretation, and belongs downstream. An extension cell is a RANGE (`dd-mm-yyyy - dd-mm-yyyy`, a start and a new end date), so each extension has a `_start` and an `_end`. Karnataka lists 47 Bengaluru Urban COVID-19 extensions with a start and no end, so `_end` is null while `_start` is set. `registration_no` is null for a project that has an acknowledgement number but was never registered. The `key` therefore uses the identifier the portal assigns first (Karnataka's acknowledgement number), so it stays the same when a registration number is later issued. Haryana lists no acknowledgement number and prints `NA` as the Project ID of 37 Gurugram projects, so its key uses the registration certificate number, which is unique across both listings.
